tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved by the letter of §3.1 but structurally contested. Rank 8 > 3, and a conditioning ingredient does precede the marker (Myristyl Alcohol @3, a long-chain fatty alcohol named in R1's list), so neither §3.1 anomaly condition is met. However, no cationic surfactant of any kind precedes the marker, and this is a low-water solvent architecture (Propylene Glycol @1, Alcohol denat. @2, Aqua only @5) in which a fragrance level above 1% is entirely plausible. A reviewer who read 'conditioning ingredient' as 'cationic conditioning agent' would set tail_marker: unresolved. See AP-02-BONDTAIL for both readings and their consequences.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 5575f0ae…), above-tail ranks 1–7; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: The mechanical §9.1 signal count reaches two, but the counting rule presupposes an aqueous emulsion in which rank position reports structural role. This is a low-water solvent system whose first two ranks carry no care payload at all, which is a material counter-signal against the `high` conjunct. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: Myristyl Alcohol (rank 3) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three of the full list
Dicaprylyl Carbonate (rank 4) and Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride (rank 7) — two distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail
Propylene Glycol (rank 1) and Alcohol denat. (rank 2) — solvents, not care payload
Aqua (rank 5) — water is only the fifth-listed ingredient
Cetrimonium Chloride (rank 9) — the sole cationic surfactant, in the tail
Cetyl Alcohol (rank 15) — in the tail
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 (≥2 distinct cationics above tail) = NOT satisfied; there are zero. S2 (long-chain fatty alcohol at rank 2 or 3 of the full list) = satisfied by Myristyl Alcohol @3, which R1's fatty-alcohol enumeration names explicitly. S3 (≥2 distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above tail) = satisfied by Dicaprylyl Carbonate @4 + Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride @7. Mechanical count = 2 of 3, which points at `high`; the `high` threshold's second conjunct ('no material counter-signal') then fails on the architecture ground below, dropping the value to the `moderate` bucket.
thresholdReasoning: `high` is refused despite the mechanical count: §9.1 sets `high` at ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} AND no material counter-signal. The material counter-signal is that D1's ruled semantics — 'overall conditioning/treatment intensity from structural INCI position only (cationic count and rank, fatty-alcohol rank, lipid-above-tail breadth)' — presuppose an emulsion where descending rank tracks the care architecture. Here ranks 1, 2 and 5 are propylene glycol, denatured alcohol and water; the entire cationic conditioning system is below the marker. Reading this formula as the equal of a three-signal butter mask would be a scale failure, not a scale result.

Clears `moderate`: §9.1 assigns `moderate` to 'everything else … including the unresolvable fallback'. D1's binding fallback rule requires unresolvable cases to land on `moderate` plus an entry in uncertain_fields, never on an extreme.
`low` does not apply: `low` requires none of S1/S2/S3. S2 and S3 are both satisfied on the literal reading, so the floor is not reached.
counterSignals: Low-water, solvent-led architecture: rank semantics do not carry their usual structural meaning (the counter-signal that blocks `high`).
Zero cationic surfactants above the tail — S1 is not merely unmet, the category's defining R1 baseline is entirely absent from the credited segment.
Alcohol denat. @2 is a volatile carrier with no care payload; §9.1's own principle (bottle infrastructure is not payload) applies by extension.
limitations: This is the clearest cohort case where §9.1's counting rule and §9.1's counter-signal paragraph collide: the paragraph says its named counter-signals 'never move the value in any direction', while the `high` threshold conditions on the absence of a material counter-signal. The two sentences cannot both be read literally (AP-02-COUNTERSIGNAL).
A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support (§9.1 honest limitation).

This is the only `low` weight value in the cohort, and it comes from a product that is architecturally not an emulsion at all. E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.
evidenceSignals: zero cationic surfactants above the tail (Cetrimonium Chloride is at rank 9)
Myristyl Alcohol (rank 3) — C14, shorter-chain than the cetyl/stearyl pair that defines the cetearyl class; Cetyl Alcohol itself is at rank 15, in the tail
Dicaprylyl Carbonate (4) and Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride (7) — light esters/triglyceride, not R4b
no butter, hydrogenated fat, occlusive hydrocarbon, or silicone at any rank
claim 'silikonfrei' — confirmed by the list, but proves nothing about lightness (§9.2 counter-signal)
weightPotential.derivation: §9.2 `low` anchor = a single cationic species AND no cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three AND no R4b heavy lipid above the tail. First conjunct: zero cationics above the tail, read as satisfying 'a single … species' a fortiori. Second: Myristyl Alcohol @3 is C14 and is not read as cetearyl-class (§9.2 says 'cetearyl-class', narrower than §9.1 S2's 'long-chain fatty alcohol'). Third: no R4b lipid at any rank.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `low`: all three conjuncts of the low anchor hold.

`moderate` would apply if Myristyl Alcohol counted as cetearyl-class — the single hinge, recorded in AP-02-MYRISTYL. It is not selected because §9.2 deliberately names the cetearyl class (C16/C18) rather than repeating §9.1's broader 'long-chain fatty alcohol' phrase, and because every other above-tail signal points the same way.
`high` does not apply: the required base needs ≥2 distinct cationics above the tail; there are zero.
§9.2 conflict fallback is not engaged: it protects against encoding uncertainty as a restrictive `high`, and this value is `low`, which widens rather than narrows the thickness prior.
counterSignals: §9.1 S2 and §9.2's low anchor use different phrases for the same slot ('long-chain fatty alcohol' vs 'cetearyl-class fatty alcohol'), and this product is the one place in the cohort where the difference changes an answer.
'silikonfrei' positioning: recorded as claim context only; silicone-free is not lightness evidence.
limitations: The `low` value is genuinely earned here but only because the product is not a conventional mask emulsion; across the rest of the cohort the `low` anchor proved unreachable (see AP-WEIGHT-LOW-UNREACHABLE in the summary).

adjudicationPoints.title: Named bond chemistry above the tail: the standard's own anchor chemistry, one rank band from a two-step swing
adjudicationPoints.body: This formula carries the exact gluconamide pair that lexicon family 6 names as the canonical positive (Hydroxypropylgluconamide + Hydroxypropylammonium Gluconate), at ranks 11 and 12, with tail_index = 8. Reading A, applied here and mandated by §3.1's mechanical cut plus R7's 'bonding ingredient found only in the tail' non-qualifier: bond_route = none, repair_support_level = low, damage_fit = healthy + moderately_damaged, primary_focus = lightness. Reading B, available if a reviewer treats the tail marker as unresolved because no CATIONIC conditioning ingredient precedes Parfum and because a low-water solvent system plausibly carries fragrance above 1%: the credited segment would extend to the preservative block (Benzyl Alcohol @21), placing the pair, Cetrimonium Chloride @9 and Hydrolyzed Keratin @13 above the tail. That yields bond_route = gluconamide, repair_support_level = HIGH, damage_fit = moderately_damaged + highly_damaged, S1 satisfied, and `repair` available as primary focus. Reading B is not a small correction: it is a two-step move on the profile's most consequential field and it changes the product's whole matching identity. The standard cannot leave this to reviewer taste. Two candidate fixes, neither adopted here: (i) state explicitly that §3.1's 'before any conditioning ingredient' means before any CATIONIC conditioning species, which would put this product into the unresolved branch; (ii) add a low-water/non-emulsion architecture branch to §3.1, since the tail-marker proxy was derived from aqueous lamellar systems and this is not one.

adjudicationPoints.title: §9.1's counter-signal paragraph and its `high` threshold contradict each other
adjudicationPoints.body: The `high` threshold reads '≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} satisfied AND no material counter-signal'. The counter-signal paragraph three lines later reads 'None of these move the value in any direction'. If the enumerated counter-signals genuinely never move a value, the `high` threshold's second conjunct can only be satisfied by counter-signals that are NOT enumerated — which makes the conjunct an unbounded reviewer discretion in a standard whose stated purpose is blind repeatability. This product is where the contradiction bites: the mechanical count says `high`, and the reason to refuse it (low-water architecture defeating rank semantics) is not on the enumerated list. Recommend the standard either enumerate the architecture-level counter-signals that may block `high` or delete the conjunct.

adjudicationPoints.title: 'long-chain fatty alcohol' (§9.1 S2) vs 'cetearyl-class fatty alcohol' (§9.2) are different tests for the same slot
adjudicationPoints.body: Myristyl Alcohol (C14) satisfies §9.1 S2, which names it explicitly in R1's list, but is not cetearyl-class (C16/C18) for §9.2's low/high anchors. Applying both phrases literally is what produces this product's unusual pairing of conditioning_level `moderate` with weight_potential `low`. If the two phrases were meant to be the same test, weight_potential becomes `moderate`, hair_thickness_fit widens to include coarse, texture_fit widens to include curly, and `lightness` becomes unreachable — taking the cohort's only `lightness` and only `low` weight with it. The standard should say whether the classes are deliberately different.

adjudicationPoints.title: §9.5.1's `nonspecific` resolution path and §9.5.2's step ordering can both be live at once
adjudicationPoints.body: §9.5.1 states that a `nonspecific` verdict 'resolves to `general` (or to `smoothing` …), never to `moisture` and never to `repair`'. §9.5.2 tests `lightness` at step 3, before the moisture test and long before the general fallback. Here the verdict is `nonspecific` and a step-3 route cleared, so the primary focus is `lightness` — a value §9.5.1's resolution sentence does not contemplate. The two rules are not in conflict on the outcome, but the standard should say that §9.5.1's resolution sentence governs only the residual case after steps 3–7 have failed.

assumptionNotes: Reviewer policy applied to every record in this lane: §3.1's hard cut determines above-tail membership without exception; the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution is applied only as a confidence modifier and never moves a value.
